nonagon.context: A regular polygon with nine equal straight sides standing on one flat edge. Used in geometry lessons, shape pickers and polygon tools.

dodecagon.context: A regular polygon with twelve short straight sides, close to a circle, with its centre marked. Used in geometry lessons, polygon tools and shape pickers.

isosceles-triangle.context: A tall triangle with a tick mark on each of its two equal slanted sides. Used in geometry lessons about triangle types and equal sides.

scalene-triangle.context: A lopsided triangle whose three sides carry one, two and three tick marks to show they are all different lengths. Used in geometry lessons on classifying triangles.

obtuse-triangle.context: A long flat triangle with its one wide angle, bigger than 90 degrees, marked by an arc. Used in geometry lessons on classifying triangles by angle.

kite-quadrilateral.context: A kite shaped quadrilateral with a short top and long bottom, its two diagonals crossing at right angles. Used in geometry lessons about quadrilaterals and their diagonals.

squircle.context: A superellipse shape halfway between a square and a circle, with straight sides blending into smooth corners. Used for app icon masks, avatars, buttons and shape tools.

annulus.context: A flat ring between two circles that share the same centre, with the centre point marked. Used in geometry lessons on ring area, and for washers, rings and donut shapes.

quarter-circle.context: A quarter of a circle: two straight radii at a right angle joined by a curved arc, with the centre corner marked. Used for sectors, quadrants and 90 degree turns.

deltoid-curve.context: A curved triangle with three sharp cusps and three sides that bend inward. Used in geometry and calculus topics about roulette curves and hypocycloids.

lune-shape.context: A crescent shaped region left over where one circle is overlapped by another, with the hidden arc of the second circle shown. Used in geometry lessons on circle areas and set difference.

arbelos.context: A large semicircle with two smaller semicircles cut out along the same base line, leaving a curved knife shape. Used in classic geometry problems and history of maths topics.

concave-polygon.context: An arrowhead shaped polygon with one corner pushed inward, its reflex angle marked with an arc. Used in geometry lessons comparing convex and concave shapes.

pentagram.context: A five pointed star drawn with crossing straight lines, with the small pentagon at its centre outlined. Used in geometry, golden ratio lessons and star polygon topics.

heptagram.context: A seven pointed star drawn with straight lines that cross each other and leave a small heptagon in the middle. Used in geometry lessons on star polygons.

octagram.context: An eight pointed star made from two overlapping squares, one turned 45 degrees, with an octagon at its centre. Used in geometry, tiling patterns and decorative star motifs.

tetrahedron.context: A triangular pyramid with four triangular faces, drawn in 3D with its hidden back edge dashed. Used in solid geometry lessons, chemistry and 3D modelling.

cuboid.context: A long rectangular box in 3D showing its front, top and side faces. Used in geometry lessons on volume and surface area, and for boxes, blocks and packaging.

parallelepiped.context: A slanted box whose six faces are all parallelograms, leaning to one side in 3D. Used in solid geometry, vector and crystal lattice topics.

pentagonal-prism.context: A prism with pentagon shaped front and back faces joined by rectangles, drawn in 3D. Used in solid geometry lessons on prisms, volume and nets.

ellipsoid.context: A stretched sphere shown as an ellipse with a curved equator and meridian across it. Used in geometry, physics and geodesy topics about oval solids and the shape of the earth.

triangular-bipyramid.context: Two triangular pyramids joined base to base, forming a double pointed solid with a triangular waist. Used in solid geometry and chemistry for molecular shapes.

truncated-cube.context: A cube with every corner sliced off, showing triangular corner faces and octagonal faces. Used in solid geometry lessons on Archimedean solids.

cuboctahedron.context: A solid of alternating square and triangular faces, drawn as a hexagon outline with triangles and squares inside. Used in solid geometry, crystal structure and architecture topics.

truncated-octahedron.context: A solid of square and hexagonal faces, shown with a square face in front surrounded by hexagons. Used in solid geometry, space filling tilings and foam structure topics.

stellated-octahedron.context: Two interlocking tetrahedra forming an eight pointed star solid, like a 3D six pointed star. Used in solid geometry and decorative star shapes.

stellated-dodecahedron.context: A spiky star shaped solid with pentagonal pyramid spikes pointing outward. Used in solid geometry lessons on star polyhedra and in decorative stars.

square-antiprism.context: Two squares, one twisted 45 degrees above the other, joined by a band of triangles. Used in solid geometry and molecular geometry lessons.

bicone.context: A double cone: two cones joined at their round bases, forming a solid with a point at each end. Used in solid geometry, spinning tops and bead shapes.

spherical-cap.context: A dome shaped slice cut from a sphere, with a flat round base whose hidden back edge is dashed. Used in geometry lessons on volume and for domes and lenses.

paraboloid.context: A bowl shaped surface opening upward with an elliptical rim and a curved line across its side. Used in geometry and physics for parabolic dishes, mirrors and reflectors.

hyperboloid.context: An hourglass shaped tower surface pinched at the waist, with straight lines crossing between its two elliptical rims. Used in geometry, cooling towers and ruled surface topics.

hyperbolic-paraboloid.context: A saddle shaped surface drawn with a grid of curved lines, rising at two corners and dipping at the other two. Used in geometry, calculus saddle points and roof architecture.

torus-knot.context: A closed loop that winds around a hidden ring, drawn with gaps to show which strand passes over and under. Used in knot theory, topology and mathematical art.

double-torus.context: A pretzel like solid with two holes side by side. Used in topology lessons about surfaces, genus and holes.

wireframe-cube.context: A see through cube with all twelve edges drawn as lines. Used in 3D modelling, CAD, mesh and wireframe view options, and geometry lessons.

cylinder-net.context: The unfolded net of a cylinder: a rectangle with a circle above and below. Used in geometry lessons on surface area and in papercraft templates.

cone-net.context: The unfolded net of a cone: a curved fan shaped sector with a small circle for the base. Used in geometry lessons on surface area and in papercraft templates.

pyramid-net.context: The unfolded net of a square pyramid: a square with a triangle folded out from each side, like a star. Used in geometry lessons and papercraft templates.

triangular-prism-net.context: The unfolded net of a triangular prism: three rectangles in a row with a triangle above and below the middle one. Used in geometry lessons and papercraft templates.

spherical-triangle.context: A sphere outline with a curved triangle drawn on its surface, its sides bulging arcs of great circles. Used in spherical geometry, navigation and astronomy topics.

poincare-disk.context: A circle filled with curved lines that meet its edge at right angles, forming curved triangles. Used in hyperbolic geometry lessons and mathematical art.

sphere-packing.context: Equal balls stacked in a triangle on a flat line: three on the bottom, two above and one on top. Used in geometry, crystal structure and packing problem topics.

cavalieri-principle.context: Two stacks of equal coins side by side, one straight and one leaning, showing they hold the same volume. Used in geometry lessons on volume and cross sections.

right-angle.context: Two straight lines meeting at a corner at exactly 90 degrees, with a small square mark in the corner. Used in geometry, drafting and carpentry.

obtuse-angle.context: Two rays from one point spread wider than a right angle, with an arc marking the wide opening. Used in geometry lessons on types of angles.

straight-angle.context: A straight line with its middle point marked and a half circle arc above it showing 180 degrees. Used in geometry lessons on types of angles.

reflex-angle.context: Two rays from one point with a long arc sweeping around the outside, marking the angle larger than 180 degrees. Used in geometry lessons on types of angles.

complementary-angles.context: A right angle corner split into two parts by a middle ray, each part marked with its own arc. Used in geometry lessons on angle pairs that add up to 90 degrees.

supplementary-angles.context: A straight line with a ray rising from a point on it, the two angles on either side marked with arcs. Used in geometry lessons on angle pairs that add up to 180 degrees.

vertical-angles.context: Two straight lines crossing in an X with matching arcs on two opposite angles. Used in geometry lessons showing that vertically opposite angles are equal.

exterior-angle.context: A triangle with its base extended past one corner and an arc marking the outside angle formed there. Used in geometry lessons on the exterior angle theorem.

dihedral-angle.context: Two flat planes meeting along a shared edge like an open book, with an arc marking the angle between them. Used in solid geometry, chemistry bond angles and crystallography.

solid-angle.context: A cone of lines from a centre point out to a curved patch on the surface of a sphere. Used in physics and geometry topics about steradians, light and radiation.

angle-of-elevation.context: A ground line with a sight line rising to the top of a flagpole, the angle at the ground marked by an arc. Used in trigonometry lessons on heights and distances.

intersecting-lines.context: Two straight lines crossing at a slant with their single meeting point marked. Used in geometry and algebra lessons on intersections and solving equations.

segment-midpoint.context: A straight line segment with both ends and its middle point marked, each half carrying one tick to show they are equal. Used in geometry lessons on midpoints and bisecting.

collinear-points.context: Three points lying on one straight line that runs through them. Used in geometry lessons on collinearity, points and lines.

geometric-plane.context: A flat parallelogram drawn in perspective to show an endless plane, with a point on it. Used in geometry lessons on points, lines and planes in space.

normal-vector.context: An arrow standing straight up from a flat plane, with a right angle mark at its foot. Used in geometry, physics and 3D graphics for surface normals.

skew-lines.context: Two straight lines that are neither parallel nor meeting, one drawn passing behind the other with a gap. Used in solid geometry lessons on lines in 3D space.

triangle-medians.context: A triangle with three lines from each corner to the middle of the opposite side, meeting at a centre point. Used in geometry lessons on medians and the centroid.

triangle-altitude.context: A triangle with a straight line dropped from the top corner to the base, meeting it at a right angle. Used in geometry lessons on triangle height and area.

triangle-incircle.context: A triangle with a circle drawn inside it touching all three sides. Used in geometry lessons on the incircle, incentre and angle bisectors.

triangle-circumcircle.context: A triangle with a circle drawn around it through all three corners, and the circle's centre marked. Used in geometry lessons on the circumcircle and circumcentre.

similar-triangles.context: A small triangle and a larger triangle of the same shape side by side, with matching angle arcs. Used in geometry lessons on similarity, scale and proportion.

congruent-triangles.context: Two identical triangles side by side with matching tick marks on their corresponding sides. Used in geometry lessons on congruence and proofs.

thales-theorem.context: A triangle inside a semicircle, its long side the diameter and its third corner on the arc, with a right angle mark. Used in geometry lessons on Thales' theorem and inscribed angles.

circle-chord.context: A circle with a straight line joining two points on its edge, not passing through the centre, which is marked. Used in geometry lessons on circle parts.

circle-diameter.context: A circle with a straight line through its centre from edge to edge, with both ends and the centre marked. Used in geometry lessons on diameter, radius and circumference.

tangent-circles.context: Two circles of different sizes touching at exactly one point, which is marked. Used in geometry lessons on tangency and circle theorems.

inscribed-polygon.context: A regular hexagon drawn inside a circle with every corner touching it, and the centre marked. Used in geometry lessons on inscribed and cyclic polygons.
